raw_response: {"sentences":[{"text":"Settle in.","source_id":"GLUE_PACING","source_type":"glue","stop_idx":0},{"text":"You're starting on the Île de la Cité, right at the Pont Neuf — take a moment and take it in.","source_id":"SYNTHESIZED_OPENER","source_type":"glue","stop_idx":0},{"text":"Henri IV was one of Paris's first great town-planners, and he took such an interest in this bridge that he'd come to inspect it himself — once delighting the workmen by taking a flying leap clean over an unfinished arch.","source_id":"1fbeb1b3-ce04-44eb-ad7c-dcd624059a0a","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0},{"text":"He was building something radical.","source_id":"4cb9c5a0-f2ec-47ea-8afb-ae44d53fe06a","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0},{"text":"Despite its name — Pont Neuf, the New Bridge — it's the oldest bridge still standing in Paris, twelve graceful arches, the first here made of stone and left free of the houses that had crowded every bridge before it.","source_id":"1fbeb1b3-ce04-44eb-ad7c-dcd624059a0a","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0,"also_cites":["4cb9c5a0-f2ec-47ea-8afb-ae44d53fe06a"]},{"text":"Halfway across, a statue of the king who built it still marks the spot.","source_id":"1fbeb1b3-ce04-44eb-ad7c-dcd624059a0a","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0},{"text":"That first statue didn't last.","source_id":"968b7287-51a9-4e51-924b-5a9f57cebdbe","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0,"also_cites":["7407276f-8817-4a51-83c7-da763dc9b514"]},{"text":"It was torn down and melted in 1792, during the Revolution.","source_id":"968b7287-51a9-4e51-924b-5a9f57cebdbe","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0,"also_cites":["7407276f-8817-4a51-83c7-da763dc9b514"]},{"text":"When the Bourbons came back it was rebuilt in 1818 by public subscription, recast from a surviving mould of the original — the bronze scavenged by melting down a statue of the general Louis Charles Antoine Desaix.","source_id":"968b7287-51a9-4e51-924b-5a9f57cebdbe","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0},{"text":"And before the new Henri IV was sealed shut, the sculptor François-Frédéric Lemot slipped four boxes inside it: a history of Henri IV's life, a 17th-century parchment certifying the original statue, a document on how the new one had been commissioned, and the full list of everyone who'd chipped in to pay for it.","source_id":"968b7287-51a9-4e51-924b-5a9f57cebdbe","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0},{"text":"He wasn't the only one hiding things — the anti-Royalist who cast the replacement smuggled a little statuette of Napoleon into the horse's belly, found only recently during restoration.","source_id":"7407276f-8817-4a51-83c7-da763dc9b514","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0},{"text":"For centuries this was the loudest place in Paris: the semicircular bays along the parapet were market stalls, crowded with teeth-pullers, quack doctors, dog-barbers and flower-sellers, while acrobats and actors worked the passing crowds.","source_id":"4cb9c5a0-f2ec-47ea-8afb-ae44d53fe06a","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0,"also_cites":["ef2eb2f7-4c6b-4aec-9e51-7dc52a93b2d4"]},{"text":"It grew so grand in scale and length that it soon became a symbol of the city itself.","source_id":"ef2eb2f7-4c6b-4aec-9e51-7dc52a93b2d4","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0},{"text":"Look along the quais on both banks now, at those rows of green boxes.","source_id":"GLUE_STAGING","source_type":"glue","stop_idx":0},{"text":"Those are the bouquinistes, that quintessentially Parisian way of selling books and prints — and the very first of them set up right here on the Pont Neuf.","source_id":"49ed2076-f1ba-4c30-a1c8-2eaf2eaab3d7","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0},{"text":"Just off the bridge, at the Place Dauphine, there was once an art show worth catching.","source_id":"70806017-6a80-4dde-be41-aa0d0ce7928a","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0},{"text":"Every year on the Petite Fête-Dieu — the 'Small Corpus Christi,' eight days after the main feast — young painters hung their canvases here, between six in the morning and noon.","source_id":"70806017-6a80-4dde-be41-aa0d0ce7928a","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0},{"text":"It was an unofficial salon, a rare chance for unknowns to be noticed, a forerunner of the Salon des Refusés that would later spark the Impressionists.","source_id":"70806017-6a80-4dde-be41-aa0d0ce7928a","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0},{"text":"In 1720 a twenty-two-year-old, the son of the man who kept the king's billiard tables, showed an antique bas-relief.","source_id":"70806017-6a80-4dde-be41-aa0d0ce7928a","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0},{"text":"The painter J.-B. Vanloo stopped, studied it a long while, found real qualities in it, bought it, and took the young man under his wing.","source_id":"70806017-6a80-4dde-be41-aa0d0ce7928a","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0},{"text":"Eight years later that unknown was Vanloo's colleague at the Academy of Painting.","source_id":"70806017-6a80-4dde-be41-aa0d0ce7928a","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0},{"text":"His name was Jean-Baptiste-Siméon Chardin.","source_id":"70806017-6a80-4dde-be41-aa0d0ce7928a","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0},{"text":"Take the steps beside the statue down to the Square du Vert-Galant — a calm spot now, but this is where Jacques de Molay, the last Grand Master of the Templars, was burned at the stake, cursing the kings of France as the flames consumed him.","source_id":"1cc3a923-e93c-490f-9dc5-55cb6a79c465","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0}]}
